cards.title: Shipping Zones, Flat Rate vs Free-Over-Threshold, and Shipping Classes
cards.summary: Structure shipping by zone, decide between flat-rate and a free-shipping minimum, and use Shipping Classes to charge more for heavy or bulky items.
cards.use_when: You are setting shipping charges for a WooCommerce store and need to handle multi-region rates plus oversized/heavy products without losing margin.

cards.title: Automated Sales Tax with WooCommerce Tax
cards.summary: Enable WooCommerce Tax (powered by TaxJar), set the store address, pick origin- vs destination-based calculation, and add reduced/zero rates per category.
cards.use_when: You need correct sales tax across US states or other jurisdictions without hand-maintaining every rate table, or you sell goods with special tax treatment.

cards.title: Elementor Responsive Controls for Product and Landing Pages
cards.summary: Use Elementor flexbox container settings and device toggles to hide, realign, or swap background images per viewport instead of shipping one desktop layout to mobile shoppers.
cards.use_when: Your store pages look fine on desktop but cramped, overlapped or unreadable on mobile/tablet, and you need a mobile merchandising fix inside the builder.

cards.title: Pre-Launch Store Configuration Checklist (Topic Map)
cards.summary: A four-part coverage map for a WooCommerce build — domain/email, store configuration, payments/tax, and shipping profiles — to verify nothing was skipped before launch.
cards.use_when: You are auditing a WooCommerce store before going live and want to confirm each configuration area is actually done rather than assumed.

cards.title: WooCommerce baseline store configuration order
cards.summary: Sequence for standing up a WooCommerce store: deactivate/delete default plugins, set profile, disable comments, install an ecommerce theme with starter site, then configure products, payments, shipping and tax.
cards.use_when: Launching a new WooCommerce store or deciding what to configure first before adding real products and taking live payments.

cards.title: Simple product configuration in WooCommerce
cards.summary: Field-by-field setup of a WooCommerce simple product, including pricing, sale schedule, inventory rules, shipping dimensions, upsells/cross-sells and category/brand assignment.
cards.use_when: Adding a single-SKU product to a WooCommerce catalog, or auditing an existing product page for missing inventory, shipping or cross-sell data.

cards.title: Variable product setup for size and color options
cards.summary: How to build a WooCommerce variable product so shoppers can select attributes such as color and size, with per-variation price, stock and image.
cards.use_when: Adding apparel, footwear or any product sold in multiple sizes, colors or materials, or when shoppers cannot currently select a variant on the PDP.

cards.title: Upsell vs cross-sell placement in WooCommerce
cards.summary: Distinguish WooCommerce upsells (on the current product page) from cross-sells (offered at cart/checkout) and pick which products to place where.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a product page or cart to raise average order value with complementary items.

cards.title: Elementor container and flexbox layout for ecommerce pages
cards.summary: Using Elementor containers with flexbox direction, justify-content and per-column width to build clean product and landing layouts that adapt across devices.
cards.use_when: Building or fixing a homepage, category or landing page layout in Elementor — e.g. getting two buttons to sit side by side or making an image column narrower than a text column.

cards.title: Starter-site import and why to remove conflicting plugins
cards.summary: Importing an ecommerce starter template (theme options, widgets, content and plugins) to get a functioning store skeleton fast, and cleaning up pre-installed plugins first to avoid broken imports.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new store quickly and needing a working shop layout — header, hero, category blocks, product grid — before replacing demo content with real products.

cards.title: Header settings that block page building and product imagery
cards.summary: Two theme-customizer header toggles — sticky header and transparent header — that interfere with page building and hero images, and when to switch them off.
cards.use_when: Troubleshooting an Elementor editing experience where the menu collides with the builder, or a hero image pushing up under the menu and hiding content.

cards.title: Responsive optimization pass across desktop, tablet and mobile
cards.summary: Per-device layout review in Elementor: centering flex content, swapping background images, applying overlays for text contrast, resizing text and hiding elements that break small screens.
cards.use_when: Doing the mobile/tablet pass on a store homepage, category page or landing page before launch, or fixing text that is illegible over an image on small screens.

cards.title: Elementor element editing, copy-paste style and AI page drafts
cards.summary: Working efficiently inside Elementor: the content/style/advanced tab model, duplicating elements and columns, copying style between same-type elements, and using Elementor AI to draft a page quickly.
cards.use_when: Building a reusable store page (About, Team, landing section) and needing to keep typography, colors and spacing consistent without restyling each element by hand.

cards.title: Creating pages, menus and dropdown navigation for a store
cards.summary: Adding WooCommerce pages such as About/Team, assigning them to the site menu, building dropdown submenus and adding external custom links (e.g. a community URL).
cards.use_when: Building out an online store's site structure — adding an Our Team or Services page, organizing the navigation under shop and contact, or linking to an off-site channel.

cards.title: WooCommerce admin surfaces for running the store after launch
cards.summary: Which WooCommerce admin screens exist and what each one answers for a store operator: orders, customers, coupons, reports and the upgraded analytics view.
cards.use_when: Setting up the operational side of a WooCommerce store — reviewing orders, tracking customers, issuing coupons and checking sales reporting after launch.

cards.title: Create variable products with size/color attributes and variation images
cards.summary: Build a variable product by defining attributes first, generating variations, then assigning per-variation image and price so the PDP swaps visuals by customer selection.
cards.use_when: Setting up a product with multiple options (sizes, colors) on the PDP so customers see the correct image and price per choice.

cards.title: Configure selling locations, shipping locations and customer location sensibly
cards.summary: Restrict selling to your actual markets and base the default customer location on the shop address rather than geolocation.
cards.use_when: Configuring store-wide General settings on a new store so checkout country fields and shipping match where you actually do business.

cards.title: Decide add-to-cart redirect behavior and product review permissions
cards.summary: Configure whether adding to cart diverts users to the cart page and whether reviews require a verified purchase or allow open reviews.
cards.use_when: Setting up Products settings on a multi-product store to reduce cart-page bounce and choose a review policy.

cards.title: Set tax calculation basis correctly by origin vs destination state
cards.summary: Choose shop-base address vs customer shipping address for tax calculation depending on whether your state is an origin-based sales-tax state.
cards.use_when: Configuring WooCommerce tax settings before going live in the US, to avoid collecting tax on the wrong basis.

cards.title: Use reduced tax rates for special product classes
cards.summary: Create a reduced tax class (e.g. 0% for digital goods) and assign it to specific products so mixed catalogs are taxed correctly.
cards.use_when: Selling a catalog mixing physical and digital (or otherwise differently taxed) items on one store.

cards.title: Automate tax rates with the WooCommerce Tax plugin
cards.summary: Install and connect the official WooCommerce Tax plugin to pull calculated rates from a live tax service instead of maintaining rows manually.
cards.use_when: You want hands-off sales-tax rates across many jurisdictions instead of hand-building standard and reduced rate rows.

cards.title: Build shipping zones with free shipping, flat rate and local pickup
cards.summary: Create a shipping zone, then layer free-shipping thresholds, a flat rate and local pickup as selectable methods at checkout.
cards.use_when: Setting up shipping options for a store that ships to specific countries or regions.

cards.title: Charge per-product shipping with shipping classes and per-class calculation
cards.summary: Create shipping classes for bulky or heavy items and set the flat-rate method to charge per class so large items cost more to ship.
cards.use_when: Your catalog contains items with very different shipping costs (small apparel vs heavy/bulky goods) and you need item-level pricing.

cards.title: Connect Stripe and PayPal payment gateways
cards.summary: Add card and PayPal payments by installing the recommended gateway plugins, creating the merchant accounts, and connecting them to the store.
cards.use_when: Enabling card and PayPal checkout on a new WooCommerce store.

cards.title: Run a test order to verify shipping, tax and checkout end to end
cards.summary: Place a live checkout with test card details to confirm free-shipping thresholds, taxes and gateway behavior before launch.
cards.use_when: Pre-launch QA of checkout, shipping options and tax configuration in a new store.

cards.title: Manage and fulfill orders, issue refunds, and understand the customer My Account page
cards.summary: Locate orders, mark them complete to notify the customer, process refunds from the order screen, and confirm what customers can self-serve.
cards.use_when: Post-purchase operations: fulfilling orders, handling refund requests, and supporting customer self-service.

cards.title: Organize product categories and handle undeletable defaults
cards.summary: Clean up imported categories, keep only what you need, and repurpose the undeletable default category instead of leaving it unused.
cards.use_when: Tidying catalog navigation and category structure after a theme import on a new store.

cards.title: Check email deliverability and customize transactional emails
cards.summary: Ensure customer order emails actually send by configuring SMTP, and optionally customize email templates with a free builder plugin.
cards.use_when: After store setup, before launch, and when customers report missing order emails.

cards.title: Tune coupon and review settings for a workable default configuration
cards.summary: Enable coupons, set measurement units and review permissions so the store behaves correctly from day one.
cards.use_when: Final pass through WooCommerce Products and General settings before launch.

cards.title: What the Meta Conversions API Gateway actually is
cards.summary: A hybrid setup where the client-side pixel fires as usual and also relays the same event to a first-party subdomain gateway that forwards it to Meta's Conversions API.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to add server-side conversion tracking to an ecommerce store when you have no developer resources and are considering the Meta CAPI Gateway instead of a full server-side tag manager.

cards.title: Why the CAPI Gateway fails against ad blockers
cards.summary: Because the gateway call is triggered by the client-side pixel, anything that blocks the pixel also blocks the server-side relay, defeating the main reason to adopt server-side tracking.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether the Meta CAPI Gateway will recover conversions lost to ad blockers and browser privacy extensions on your storefront before you invest in it.

cards.title: Deduplicating pixel and Conversions API events with matching IDs
cards.summary: The gateway auto-attaches the same event ID to both the browser pixel event and the server-side event so Meta can deduplicate the pair.
cards.use_when: Verifying your conversion tracking after installing the CAPI Gateway, or diagnosing double-counted purchases and inflated conversion counts.

cards.title: Setting up the gateway via Stape: pricing and subdomain mapping
cards.summary: A cheaper third-party host (Stape) provisions the Meta CAPI gateway, but the real setup step is mapping a dedicated CNAME subdomain so the pixel has a first-party endpoint.
cards.use_when: Provisioning the Meta CAPI Gateway for a store and mapping a first-party subdomain as a low-cost alternative to Meta's own gateway hosting.

cards.title: What true server-side tagging buys over the gateway
cards.summary: A full server-side setup can rewrite request URLs via a custom loader for higher delivery rates and can extend cookie lifetime, which the gateway does not do.
cards.use_when: Choosing between the Meta CAPI Gateway and a full server-side (e.g. GTM server container) setup for a store that needs durable attribution and cookie longevity.

cards.title: Measure purchase conversion rate, not raw key event rate
cards.summary: GA4's 'key events' bundle purchases with other actions, so you must manually filter to the purchase event before reading any conversion rate.
cards.use_when: Judging whether your store's or a channel's conversion rate is healthy before making merchandising or media-spend decisions.

cards.title: Find conversion rate by traffic channel
cards.summary: Customize the Traffic Acquisition report to add session key event rate filtered to purchase so you can compare conversion performance across organic, CPC and email.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to shift acquisition budget or fix a channel that drives traffic but no sales.

cards.title: Read engaged sessions as a traffic-relevance signal
cards.summary: GA4 counts a session as engaged when it lasts longer than 10 seconds, making it a quick relevance check on the traffic you are buying or earning.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing whether paid or organic traffic is actually reaching a page that matches the visitor's intent.

cards.title: Compare product-page conversion rates in the Landing Pages report
cards.summary: Add the purchase-filtered session key event rate to the Landing Pages report to see which product pages convert and which are leaking.
cards.use_when: Deciding which product pages need new copy, photography or price tests, or whether a page's traffic is simply mismatched.

cards.title: Diagnose funnel drop-off with the Purchase Journey report
cards.summary: The Monetization -> Purchase Journey report shows drop-off between session start, product view, add to cart, checkout and purchase so you can localise friction.
cards.use_when: Investigating where shoppers abandon so you can decide whether to fix navigation, cart, pricing or checkout trust.

cards.title: Segment traffic by channel and medium together
cards.summary: Adding the medium dimension to the Traffic Acquisition report gives a second layer of detail, separating CPC from paid social and identifying specific senders like your email platform.
cards.use_when: Working out which specific paid or owned channel is producing sessions, before shifting budget or cadence.

cards.title: Customize and save GA4 reports instead of reading defaults
cards.summary: Default GA4 tables omit the metrics you actually need; adding metrics under Customize Report -> Metrics and saving the view is the core workflow.
cards.use_when: Setting up a repeatable weekly reporting routine you do not want to rebuild each time.

cards.title: Use GA4 to fill gaps Shopify analytics leaves
cards.summary: GA4's traffic-source and per-page detail exceeds what the Shopify dashboard reports, so treat GA4 as the channel and page diagnostic layer and Shopify as the order-level view.
cards.use_when: Deciding which analytics tool to check for a given question about traffic or page performance.

cards.title: Read GA4's AI Insights for quick answers, not deep analysis
cards.summary: The Insights tool offers predefined suggested questions and short answers, useful for fast orientation when you are new to the platform.
cards.use_when: Getting a fast orientation answer such as which countries your visitors come from, before digging into a full report.

cards.title: GA4 data retention: switch from 2 months to 14 months
cards.summary: Choose a suitable retention window for ecommerce explorations; standard aggregated reports are unaffected.
cards.use_when: Setting up a fresh GA4 property or auditing an existing one before relying on it for year-over-year ecommerce reporting.

cards.title: Prevent fragmented sessions by extending GA4 session timeout
cards.summary: GA4's default 30-minute session timeout can split a single shopping journey into multiple sessions, distorting engagement and conversion metrics.
cards.use_when: Configuring a new GA4 property or investigating why session counts and conversion rates look inflated or fragmented for a store with long browse-to-purchase lag.

cards.title: Configure cross-domain tracking for checkout on a separate domain
cards.summary: If any step of a purchase journey crosses domains (e.g., a third-party checkout), analytics without cross-domain tracking will attribute the sale to a new session and lose the true source.
cards.use_when: Setting up analytics for a store whose checkout, cart, or landing flow uses a different domain than the main site — common with hosted checkouts and upsell tools.

cards.title: Filter internal office IP traffic out of GA4
cards.summary: Office and testing traffic inflates sessions and distorts conversion metrics, so define and exclude it during setup.
cards.use_when: New GA4 setup or ongoing data-quality audit for a store where staff frequently visit the site to test products, pricing, or checkout.

cards.title: Create custom GA4 events via GTM with triggers and parameters
cards.summary: Track meaningful on-page interactions (like menu link clicks) as custom GA4 events by configuring them in Google Tag Manager with precise triggers and parameters.
cards.use_when: Building out analytics for a store where default GA4 events don't capture the interactions that matter for merchandising or navigation decisions.

cards.title: Register GTM custom parameters as GA4 Custom Dimensions
cards.summary: Custom event parameters you send through GTM are invisible in GA4 reports until you register them as Custom Dimensions.
cards.use_when: After setting up a custom event (e.g., menu link clicks) and finding its parameters are not available for reporting or explorations.

cards.title: Test GA4/GTM event setup before publishing the container
cards.summary: Verify every new tracking tag in GTM Preview and GA4 DebugView before publishing, so broken tracking doesn't silently corrupt data.
cards.use_when: Any time you add or change a tracking tag for a store, before pushing the change live to all users.

cards.title: Use a single GA4 property across domains in one journey
cards.summary: When a single customer journey crosses multiple domains, the source recommends one GA4 property with cross-domain tracking rather than separate properties.
cards.use_when: Deciding property architecture for a store that uses a main site plus a separate checkout, landing, or app domain.

cards.title: Reverse-engineer the purchase path with Path Exploration
cards.summary: GA4 Path Exploration lets you start from a purchase event and work backward to see the sequence of pages and events preceding conversions.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing where buyers drop off or what pages precede a purchase, to inform merchandising and PDP/checkout improvements.

cards.title: Build Free Form tables in GA4 Explorations
cards.summary: Free Form analysis in GA4 lets you build custom cross-tabulated tables of dimensions and metrics to answer specific store questions beyond standard reports.
cards.use_when: When a store question (e.g., which products convert best by traffic source, or how a specific landing page performs) is not answerable from GA4's standard reports.

cards.title: Extend the engaged-session threshold above the 10-second default
cards.summary: GA4's default engaged-session threshold of 10 seconds understates meaningful engagement, so the source recommends raising it to at least 30 seconds.
cards.use_when: Configuring GA4 settings for a store where you want engagement metrics to reflect genuine browsing rather than momentary visits.

cards.title: Enable Google Signals for demographic audience data
cards.summary: Google Signals provides demographic reporting (age, gender, interests) and enables cross-device information in GA4.
cards.use_when: When you want demographic or interest data to guide ad targeting, creative strategy, or audience definitions for a store.

cards.title: Apply GA4 naming conventions to custom events
cards.summary: Use lowercase letters and underscores for GA4 event names to keep tracking consistent and avoid downstream reporting breaks.
cards.use_when: Creating any custom event in GA4/GTM for a store, or standardizing event names across teams and tools.

cards.title: Treat GA4 setup as a five-setting baseline for ecommerce accuracy
cards.summary: The source identifies five mandatory GA4 admin configurations to make ecommerce data trustworthy before you rely on it.
cards.use_when: Onboarding a new GA4 property or auditing an established store analytics setup before making merchandising or marketing decisions from it.

cards.title: Do not rely on AI chat assistants for GA4 technical configuration
cards.summary: The source warns that an AI analytics chat assistant hallucinated incorrect technical advice about GA4, so verify AI-generated setup guidance against GA4's actual interface.
cards.use_when: When seeking quick answers on GA4 setup or landing-page attribution issues, before applying AI-generated configuration advice to a live store property.

cards.title: Structure a GA4 account for an ecommerce store
cards.summary: Decide account, property and data stream structure based on whether your storefront, checkout and subdomains form one user journey.
cards.use_when: Setting up GA4 for a store that spans several domains (e.g. main shop domain plus a separate checkout or landing domains) and you need to decide how many properties and streams to create.

cards.title: Install the GA4 tag: CMS, hardcode, or GTM
cards.summary: Choose between a CMS tracking-ID field, developer-installed code, or Google Tag Manager for deploying GA4 on an ecommerce site.
cards.use_when: Choosing how to deploy GA4 (and later ecommerce event tags) on your storefront, especially when you lack developer time or need to add vendor tags.

cards.title: Test a GA4 tag with GTM Preview and DebugView
cards.summary: Run the GTM preview → DebugView sequence to confirm a tag fires and GA4 receives the event and its parameters before publishing.
cards.use_when: Validating any new GA4 tracking tag (ecommerce events, custom events) on your store before publishing it to live shoppers.

cards.title: Read acquisition reports: first touch vs session
cards.summary: Distinguish user acquisition (first source ever) from traffic acquisition (per session) to answer the right question about store traffic.
cards.use_when: Deciding which channel or campaign drove purchases and revenue for your store, and avoiding misreading first-touch attribution as current-session attribution.

cards.title: Use the ecommerce purchases report for product decisions
cards.summary: Read item views, add-to-carts, purchases and item revenue per product to find merchandising winners and drop-off points.
cards.use_when: Merchandising and product-selection decisions — spotting products with strong views but weak add-to-cart or purchase rates, or identifying top revenue items.

cards.title: Diagnose checkout drop-off by device or browser
cards.summary: Use the checkout journey report with breakdown dimensions to find where and on which devices/browsers shoppers abandon checkout.
cards.use_when: Optimizing the cart and checkout flow — locating funnel steps that lose the most shoppers and checking whether a specific browser/device has a technical problem.

cards.title: Landing page vs pages and screens report
cards.summary: Use the landing-page report for session entry pages and pages-and-screens for total page views, and understand why revenue in the pages report can mislead.
cards.use_when: Evaluating which entry pages (homepage, collections, checkout URL) start sessions and drive revenue, versus measuring overall page popularity.

cards.title: Mark key events and pick the right conversion metric
cards.summary: Distinguish plain events from key events (purchase, signup) and use them in acquisition and exploration reports to count real business outcomes.
cards.use_when: Deciding which ecommerce actions (purchase, newsletter signup, account creation) should count as conversions and where to read them by traffic source.

cards.title: Build a free-form exploration for product/device decisions
cards.summary: Create free-form explorations with dimensions as rows/columns and metrics as values to cross-tab store performance, e.g. revenue by country and device.
cards.use_when: Answering a specific merchandising or targeting question — e.g. which countries or device categories generate the most purchase revenue — beyond what standard reports allow.

cards.title: Mine site-search terms to find assortment gaps
cards.summary: Build a free-form exploration of site search terms and event counts to see what shoppers ask for and whether your catalogue answers it.
cards.use_when: Product selection and assortment planning — spotting search terms with high demand but no matching products, or reframing how products are named/merchandised.

cards.title: Funnel exploration: build an ecommerce funnel with breakdowns
cards.summary: Define ordered steps (view_item → add_to_cart → begin_checkout → purchase) in a funnel exploration and break them down by device to find where completion drops.
cards.use_when: Pinpointing the biggest conversion leak in your purchase path and checking whether it differs by device category.

cards.title: Path exploration: work backward from purchase or checkout events
cards.summary: Set the ending point to purchase or begin_checkout and read backward to reveal looping or confusing paths before conversion.
cards.use_when: Investigating why shoppers abandon checkout (e.g. logging in and out repeatedly) or what pages precede a purchase.

cards.title: Create and register custom events and dimensions in GA4 via GTM
cards.summary: Send a custom event (e.g. menu-link click) with parameters from GTM, then register those parameters as custom dimensions to use them in reports.
cards.use_when: Tracking a store interaction GA4 does not collect automatically — e.g. clicks on a homepage banner, nav menu, or a category tile you want to evaluate.

cards.title: Configure five settings in every new GA4 property
cards.summary: Day-one GA4 configuration: event data retention to 14 months, cross-domain tracking, session timeout, engaged-session threshold, and internal traffic exclusions.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new store property or fixing a recently created one where exploration history is short or sessions split unnaturally.

cards.title: Use Analytics Advisor cautiously for quick questions
cards.summary: The Gemini-powered Analytics Advisor answers natural-language questions about your GA4 data, but hallucinates on technical causes.
cards.use_when: Getting a fast number from your own GA4 property (e.g. purchases from organic search last week) without building an exploration.

cards.title: Demographics, tech and region reports for audience context
cards.summary: Use user attributes and tech detail reports to see where shoppers are and what they browse on, treating demographics as directional.
cards.use_when: Shaping merchandising, shipping or site-experience decisions — e.g. localising assortment by region or prioritising mobile experience.

cards.title: Set GA4 event data retention to 14 months at property creation
cards.summary: Choose a suitable retention window for ecommerce explorations; standard aggregated reports are unaffected.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new GA4 property for an ecommerce store, or auditing an existing property before doing seasonal/year-over-year merchandising and product performance analysis.

cards.title: Register all business domains for cross-domain tracking in GA4
cards.summary: List every domain your store uses in GA4 domain configuration so sessions spanning multiple properties are attributed correctly.
cards.use_when: When your ecommerce operation runs across multiple domains or subdomains (e.g., main store and a separate checkout or regional domain) and you need accurate session and conversion attribution.

cards.title: Exclude internal (employee) traffic from GA4 reports
cards.summary: Define internal traffic rules by IP and activate the data filter so staff visits do not pollute ecommerce metrics.
cards.use_when: When employees work from an office or have static IPs and you are making decisions from conversion rate, session, or product-performance reports that staff browsing would distort.

cards.title: Extend GA4 session timeout and engagement timer (source opinion)
cards.summary: The presenter recommends raising the default 30-minute session timeout and the engaged-session timer, accepting fewer but longer sessions in exchange for cleaner landing-page data.
cards.use_when: When reviewing landing-page and acquisition reports and seeing many 'not set' landing pages or sessions that break up a single shopping visit.

cards.title: Enable Google Signals to populate demographics and interests
cards.summary: Turn on Google Signals in GA4 so age, gender, and interest dimensions stop being empty, weighing advertising-feature and privacy implications first.
cards.use_when: When you want demographic or interest data to segment ecommerce audiences (e.g., which age bands drive purchases) but your reports currently show no data for those dimensions.

cards.title: Configure five foundational GA4 settings in the correct order
cards.summary: A starting checklist for a new GA4 property: data retention, domain configuration, internal traffic exclusion, session timing, and Google Signals.
cards.use_when: When onboarding a new ecommerce GA4 property or auditing an existing one before trusting its conversion and product reports.
